title: Unbounded RPC can block failover and orderly worker shutdown
original_condition: In the original baseline, an established remote RPC call could wait indefinitely, including while a chain-selection mutex was held, preventing failover and orderly shutdown.
boundary_prerequisites: A stalled provider or network was sufficient; no flood was required.
current_assessment: boundedILNRPC read/evidence calls use real context cancellation, twelve-second request/four-second dial timeouts and a response limit; Worker.Close cancels that shared context. SubmitMembership and SubmitILNGovernance select a verified URL, then create txrelayer.NewTxRelayer without injecting the bounded client or worker shutdown context. Both run preflight reads through relayer.Client and then SendTransaction. The node-owned txrelayer creates its own legacy jsonrpc.NewClient. The pinned ethgo HTTP transport constructs a fasthttp client without read/write deadlines and calls Do; those defaults are unlimited. Its Close method has no cancellation effect. WithReceiptTimeout changes the sleep between receipt polls, not the timeout of GetTransactionReceipt or any other HTTP call. These are reachable worker paths: governanceExecuteLoop synchronously calls executeGovernanceJob and is part of the WaitGroup; the main loop calls tick -> trySubmissions -> trySubmit -> SubmitMembership. Worker.Close waits for them; IBFT.Close invokes it before closing the syncer. Separately, chain-selection locks still span bounded provider I/O, finality polling can continue to five minutes after cancellation, and native receipt polling has a two-minute outer deadline without the worker shutdown context. Unbounded external submission/preflight I/O can still hold a worker and orderly shutdown despite read-side cancellation. Per-call or polling-loop limits on other clients do not impose deadlines on this separate transport. No live consensus stall is asserted. Current residual prerequisites: an authorized governance execution or eligible membership preflight/submission is active against an external chain and its separate legacy transport stalls. Actual consensus halt was not demonstrated.

boundary_prerequisites: A sponsor payout is initially mined successfully, then reorganized or inconsistently reported before the adopted native finality threshold. The original durable confirmed state suppresses a legitimate later payment/recovery path.
current_assessment: Both immediate receipt handling and submitted-grant reconciliation invoke verifiedSponsorFinality before recording confirmed. The helper requires a successful matching receipt, a native head covering the receipt, matching canonical receipt block hashes and a freshly observed successful receipt. Base/Arbitrum use safe; XGRChain uses latest with two additional blocks. Unsupported or insufficient evidence retains submitted status and does not authorize duplicate payment.

title: UI can present deferred native principal as completed payout without a claim action
original_condition: The native router deliberately treats a fully reserved deferred payout as successful message handling. Presentation equates final Mailbox handling with beneficiary balance receipt, and does not discover or expose the beneficiary-only withdrawal.
boundary_prerequisites: Authenticated inbound native XGR transfer to a recipient whose receive/fallback rejects or exceeds the bounded payout gas. No malicious BLS signer or transport replay is needed.
current_assessment: The native router deliberately treats a fully reserved deferred payout as successful message handling. Presentation equates final Mailbox handling with beneficiary balance receipt, and does not discover or expose the beneficiary-only withdrawal. A user can see an apparently completed principal payout while value remains in router custody and requires a claim. A general smart wallet can call the claim function itself or direct payout to another address; a contract with no arbitrary-call or claim facility may be unable to recover. External ownership of a contract does not authorize an EOA to claim its balance.

title: Positive microfees make transfers without sponsorship promises eligible to starve owed grants
original_condition: Older operations with any positive service fee could occupy the limited sponsor candidate worklist even though no immutable gas promise existed. Rejected no-promise rows stayed ahead of later payable grants and could repeatedly consume the candidate window.
boundary_prerequisites: Enough older valid positive-fee operations without gas commitments precede a genuine owed sponsored transfer. Creating those source operations can have a cost; arbitrary public writes to the database are not assumed.
current_assessment: The current candidate query inner-joins the exact payer/source/adapter/quote nonce/fee intent and its immutable commitment rows before ORDER BY and LIMIT 120. No-promise positive-fee transfers cannot consume that candidate window. Grant execution independently verifies the matching finalized source receipt and immutable promise.
